$comment: The source of sf-button's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/button (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

appearance.summary: How the button looks. Surface reads the neutral alpha ramp: a faint fill and a border.

scheme.summary: Which colour family the control takes. on-surface-variant is the on-surface family one step quieter: the fill and the edge of on-surface, the label and the icons in --sf-on-surface-variant (a search trigger that reads like a field). What the control is about is the status axis; a status set there wins over this.

status.summary: What the control is about, in the shared status vocabulary. The only one a control paints today is `error`, the destructive one: a control that deletes, discards or cannot be undone.

text-position.summary: How the label aligns inside a button wider than its content: start, center or end (the text-align utility on the label).

text.summary: Visible button text when no text slot is provided.

segment.summary: The button's place in a joined group: start, middle or end squares the corners it shares with its neighbours; empty: a standalone button.

icon-position.summary: Placement for the single icon shortcut.

loading.summary: Loading state: the spinner at the icon's size in place of the start icon (else the end icon); without an icon it lies over the label, which keeps its place, so the width does not change. The spinner takes the page's look (data-sf-spinner). The inner button is unavailable while it loads.

form.summary: The id of the form the inner button submits or resets, as a native button's form attribute: a button outside the form (a wizard's footer) submits it. Not written on a link.

name.summary: The name the inner button submits its value under, as a native button's name.

value.summary: The value the inner button submits under name when it is the submitter (next, skip).

href.summary: An address: the button draws a link (an <a href>) with the button's look; role link, Enter and the browser's link keys follow it. A relative address, a fragment, http(s), mailto or tel; any other scheme draws a button. native-type, expanded and pressed do not apply; disabled or loading, the link has no href and says aria-disabled.

target.summary: Where a link (href) opens, as an <a target>: _blank opens a new tab. Not written on a button.

rel.summary: The link's relation, as an <a rel>. A link that opens in a new tab (target _blank) with no rel says noopener noreferrer, so the new page cannot reach this one. Not written on a button.

shortcut.summary: A key combination drawn at the end of the button as keys, muted: words joined by +, e.g. mod+k (Cmd K on a Mac, Ctrl K elsewhere), shift+/, / or escape. mod is Cmd on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere. Also written as aria-keyshortcuts on the inner button. Empty: no keys

shortcut-listen.summary: The button listens to its shortcut on the page and is pressed by it, as by a click. A combination without mod, ctrl, alt or meta is not heard while focus is in an editable field

expanded.summary: Whether the panel this button opens is open: aria-expanded on the inner button; absent says nothing

pressed.summary: Whether this toggle button is on: aria-pressed on the inner button and the pressed look -- the primary container fill, its ink, no visible edge and the icon filled (rule C12); pressed="false" says off; absent, the button is not a toggle and nothing is said

text-pressed.summary: The label while the toggle is on, for a toggle whose label changes («В избранное» → «В избранном»). Set, the label says the state and aria-pressed is not written; the pressed look still follows pressed. Empty: the label stays the same and aria-pressed says the state

press.summary: A press: a click, Enter or Space on the inner button or link, or the shortcut-listen key; the detail is an empty object. Not sent by click() on the host, nor by a disabled or loading button.

relations.name: spinner
$comment: The spinner a loading button shows: its slot is drawn by the button sheet,
the motion by the spinner's, fetched after the page is ready.

relations.name: kbd
$comment: The keys of a shortcut: the button sheet draws their box from the kbd sheet's own
variables with the same values as fallbacks, so the first paint is right before
the kbd sheet, fetched after the page is ready, arrives.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-button for the shim (stands/18-aliases-ci/alias.mjs, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split / detail-adds (a detail adapter, refused by the shim), attribute-and-property, method, property, manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), host-attribute (no shim), retired.

rows.note: stays a host attribute, read by the base (§3.1, §4.8); no shim
the legacy axis name; the shim maps the attribute and the property
rows.summary: Legacy name for appearance, still honoured. See contracts/public-api-axes.json.

rows.note: journal attribute-icon-left-right-to-start-end; icon-start wins when both are given
journal attribute-icon-left-right-to-start-end; icon-end wins when both are given
journal attribute-tightness-to-spacing; its words are spacing's value aliases below, spacing wins when both are given
the physical name the template read as start
the physical name the template read as end

x-summary: A native button with Framework presentation: size, appearance, colour role or status, optional start and end icons, spacing and radius. loading sets aria-busy and disables it against repeated activation.
x-renamed: settings.aria-label: a host attribute, read by the base, never a setting (§3.1)
x-decisions: a11y-role: button, the native <button> the template draws (the host is display:contents and takes no role). The name is the text (the setting, a text child or the text slot), else the host's aria-label, which the base passes to the native button (§3.1, §4.8).
key-effects: Tab reach. Enter and Space are the native button's own activation, not an effect of the closed list; they send press like a click, and probe.json drives Enter (gate 16).

press: the event the stands wrote as the 1.3.x target (x-target), sf-button-press with an empty detail, sent once per activation of the native button (a click, Enter, Space) and never while it is disabled or loading. The native click still bubbles as before; press is what a rule hears as <role>.press (§8, §9).

expanded: an optional boolean the stands added (x-target): present, it writes aria-expanded on the native button; absent, nothing is said. A page that wrote aria-expanded on the host keeps it: the host forwards it as before.

legacy names: type -> appearance, icon-left -> icon-start, icon-right -> icon-end and tightness -> spacing leave the settings and are dated setting aliases (aliases.json, until 2026-12-01; journal attribute-icon-left-right-to-start-end, attribute-tightness-to-spacing). The legacy values are dated value aliases: appearance ghost -> link (journal value-button-ghost-to-link), status danger and critical -> error (value-status-danger-critical-to-error), spacing low/high/highest -> compact/comfortable/spacious (tightness's words), icon-position left/right -> start/end.

icon-start and icon-end keep their own getters: an attribute written empty means «no icon here» and suppresses the icon shortcut, an absent one lets it through (null and "" differ), which a generated string setting cannot say.
aria-label is a host attribute, never a setting (§3.1); the template reads it from the host.

template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows; no template.html until the build compiles one (a copy nothing draws would drift). The host stays display:contents: geometry lives on > button.

examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (Продолжить, default primary) plus tonal, outline, link and surface, the error status, icons at the start and the end, an icon-only button with aria-label, loading, disabled and the sizes.
css-variables: the seven public variables of src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json the class sheet already reads (§6).

folder: buttons takes the tag's name, button (§3, §21, §16 item 16); the loader bundle is cl-button, cl-buttons is a Loader forward (src/core/contracts/smart-rule-forwards.v1.json) and smart/buttons/js/buttons.js a forwarding script until 2026-12-01 (change journal path-smart-buttons-to-button). The registry id follows the folder: smart.button (smart.buttons is its dated alias in the same record).
version 1.1.0: renamed members behind dated aliases and two added members (press, expanded) are a minor (§4.10, §16.20).

version 1.1.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.
version 1.1.2: the first-paint sheet list names the utility sheets its templates draw with (core.runtime 1.0.7 asks for them before the element draws: the style gate).

version 1.1.3: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.1.4: a text attribute, even an empty one, is the label: emptying it empties the button instead of falling back to a text-child label (simai.main, a toolbar clearing its labels on a narrow screen, 2026-10-28).

version 1.2.0: a minor (§4.10): the settings shortcut and shortcut-listen and the scheme value on-surface-variant are added. shortcut draws the combination at the end of the button as kbd keys (one <kbd class="sf-kbd--group"> holding a <kbd> per key, aria-hidden, the native button's aria-keyshortcuts says it), muted (--sf-on-surface-variant), with the label taking the free room (flex 1) so text-position start reads like a field. The key box is the kbd sheet's (its variables, read with the same values as fallbacks, so the first paint holds before the lazily fetched kbd sheet). shortcut-listen presses the native button (a click, so sf-button-press follows) on the combination; a combination without a modifier is not heard in an editable field, and a disabled or loading button is never pressed. on-surface-variant: the search trigger of the Docara prototypes (search-and-settings.html) wanted the on-surface family with a quieter label; the template writes both scheme classes, sf-button--on-surface and sf-button--on-surface-variant, so every on-surface rule (fill, edge, type) holds and one rule moves the label and the icon to --sf-on-surface-variant.

version 1.3.0: a minor (§4.10): the setting pressed is added (stage 1 of the component sets, duplication audit A-10). Present, the native button carries aria-pressed ("true" or "false") and, while on, the class sheet's active state, the selected look the buttons component documents for a real two-state button; absent, the button is not a toggle and nothing is said. A page that wrote aria-pressed on the host keeps it: the host forwards it as before.

version 1.4.0: a minor (§4.10): the setting href is added (visual parity of the one block editor, 2026-11-04: a button that is a link). Set, the template draws <a href> with the same classes as the native button, so the class sheet gives it the button's look; its role is link and the browser follows it (Enter, the context menu, a new tab), sf-button-press still fires on a click. accessibility.role stays button for the element without href. A relative address, a fragment, http(s), mailto and tel are taken; any other scheme (javascript:, data:) is refused and the button draws as a button. Disabled or loading, the link loses its href (not reached by Tab, not followed) and says role link and aria-disabled true. native-type, expanded and pressed are a button's words and are not written on a link.

version 1.4.1 (2026-11-07): a cap of one character is a square key -- each key carries sf-button-shortcut-key--square when its cap is one character, and the sf-button-shortcut-key--chars-N classes are gone: a modifier no longer keeps the box of its widest platform word, so ⇧ and ⌘ stand as wide as P (docs review R010). The keys on a default or tonal button take the button's own ink (component.buttons 1.3.0, R009). Settings, values and events unchanged.

version 1.5.0: a minor (§4.10): the settings form, name and value are added (sf-wizard, owner decision 2026-11-06, ui-control control/decisions/2026-11-06-sf-wizard.md): the native button carries them as a native button does, so a button outside a form submits it (form) and the server reads which button sent it (name, value) -- a wizard's footer posts the step's form with next or skip and adds no hidden field. Before, a host attribute of these names reached the native button only as an undeclared forwarded attribute. They are a button's words: a link (href) does not carry them.

version 1.5.1 (2026-11-07): the reference wording (docs review R022): press says what sends it, checked in a browser on the built bytes -- a click, Enter or Space on the inner button or link, the shortcut-listen key; the detail is an empty object; not click() on the host, not a disabled or loading button (a click() on the inner button does send it). size, disabled and loading read plainly; the control is the inner button, the docs' term, not the native one. element.dataAttributes no longer returns the style gate's sfStyleReady / sfStylePending (core.runtime 1.32.2). scheme secondary in the outline, surface and link appearances is drawn (component.buttons 1.4.0, owner decision 2026-11-07, variant A): the on-surface button's edge, fill, padding, height and states with the label and the icons in --sf-secondary; before, those three had no rule -- about 32px at size 1, no padding, the browser's text colour. One height per size at every density (component.buttons 1.4.0). Settings, values and events unchanged.

version 1.6.0 (2026-11-07): a minor (§4.10): the pressed look and the setting text-pressed (owner decision 2026-11-07, docs review R028, rule C12). A toggle that is on wears sf-button--pressed instead of the active class: the primary container fill (--sf-primary-container), no visible edge (the border keeps its width, so the height of the size does not move, and is transparent over the fill), the label and the icons in --sf-on-primary-container, and the icons filled (FILL 1) -- two cues, not colour alone, the same in both themes. Hover and press over it step the container (+4, +8 of the fill family); focus draws the ring; disabled wears the disabled look and keeps the filled icon. Public variables --sf-button-pressed-background-color and --sf-button-pressed-color colour the resting pressed look. text-pressed is the label while on, for a toggle whose label changes: the label then says the state and aria-pressed is not written (both at once read «В избранном, нажата»). A host's aria-pressed and the plain class sheet's [aria-pressed="true"] draw the same look.

version 1.6.1 (2026-11-07): a loading button's spinner draws its ring inside the icon's live area (docs review R027, owner decision C11; component.spinner 1.1.0): 20 of the 24 units, as the Material Symbol beside it, in the same icon box, so nothing around it moves; the first-paint snapshots are retaken. The settings are unchanged.

version 1.6.2 (2026-11-08): the keys a person presses are listed as the icon button lists them (msg-c84f2727): Tab reaches the button, Enter and Space press it -- the generated reference showed Tab alone; a link (href) is followed by Enter, as the href setting says. The reference describes the current button only (docs review rules D02, D03): the appearance words no longer name the former ghost, which the change journal and the alias table carry, and pressed names the rule, not a sheet's version. Settings, values, events and the drawing are unchanged.

version 1.7.0 (2026-11-08): a minor (§4.10): the settings target and rel are added (Larena after sf-wizard, msg-12cd5ef6): a link (href) writes them on its <a> as they are given, so a button-looking link can open a new tab; target _blank with no rel says rel="noopener noreferrer" and the opened page cannot reach window.opener; a rel the page writes is kept. A button (no href) writes neither. Before, the host forwarded both as undeclared attributes onto whichever control it drew -- a <button target> too -- and a new tab kept the opener. The number 1.7.0 is also held by feat/sf-kbd-r030 (sf-kbd); the dispatcher renumbers at integration.

$comment-after: The bundle's former name cl-buttons (the folder was `buttons` until standard
1.3.8 §3, §21 gave it the tag's name) is not a rule here: a rule of type
smart is a Smart component to the registry, and this one has no element. The
Loader forwards it to cl-button from src/core/contracts/

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-button when the interface needs the buttons behavior.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component

onClick.summary: Adds a listener for click on the host. Returns the element.

onFocus.summary: Adds a listener for focusin on the host. Returns the element.

onBlur.summary: Adds a listener for focusout on the host. Returns the element.

onMouseEnter.summary: Adds a listener for mouseenter on the host. Returns the element.

onMouseLeave.summary: Adds a listener for mouseleave on the host. Returns the element.

setDisabled.summary: Sets the disabled attribute when nextValue is truthy and removes it otherwise. Returns the element.

root-class.description: Extra classes applied to the inner button element.

aria-label.description: Accessible label for icon-only or custom buttons.
